name: Savassi
tagline: Boteco tables on every corner, the heart of BH nightlife
description: Savassi is the social centre of Belo Horizonte, a grid of mid-rise blocks where bar tables spill onto the pavement every evening and craft beer taps sit beside traditional botecos. Daytime brings specialty coffee, gyms, banks and the Feira da Savassi. Most visiting remote workers end up basing here.
bestFor: Nomads who want walkable nightlife, coffee and coworking in one district
pros: Best concentration of cafes and coworking in the city
Easy to meet people any night of the week
cons: Bar noise carries late on Thursday to Saturday
Among the priciest rents in Belo Horizonte
Street parking is scarce and expensive

name: Lourdes
tagline: The city's most upmarket and leafy address
description: Lourdes sits just west of Savassi and is the most upscale district in Belo Horizonte, with tree-lined streets, doorman buildings, fine dining and designer shops around Praca da Liberdade. It is quieter and greener than its neighbour while staying within easy walking distance of everything.
bestFor: Nomads with a comfortable budget who want safety and calm next to the action
pros: Feels safe to walk at night, well lit and patrolled
Quiet streets but Savassi is five minutes away
Praca da Liberdade museums and green space nearby
cons: The highest rents and restaurant prices in the city
Very little budget food or nightlife inside the district
Skews older and residential, harder to meet other nomads

name: Funcionários
tagline: Galleries, quiet cafes and a slower Savassi
description: Funcionários wraps around Savassi to the east, keeping the same walkability with a calmer feel: tree-lined residential streets, art galleries, small bookshops and cafes that stay peaceful enough to work in. Buildings are a mix of 1970s blocks and newer apartments, and rents sit slightly below Savassi.
bestFor: Remote workers who want central access but need to actually sleep at night
pros: Walk to Savassi in minutes without the bar noise
Quieter cafes that suit long working sessions
Slightly cheaper rent than Savassi or Lourdes
cons: Fewer restaurants and shops inside the district itself
Steep hills on some streets make walking hard work
Very little happens here after around 10pm

name: Santa Tereza
tagline: Hilly bohemian streets and the city's live music soul
description: Santa Tereza climbs the hills east of the centre and is where BH keeps its music: samba botecos, street art on almost every wall, and the legendary bar culture around Rua Mato Grosso and Praca Duque de Caxias. Housing is older single-storey and low-rise, and rents are the cheapest of the central options.
bestFor: Nomads chasing local culture and live music on a smaller budget
pros: Cheapest central-ish rent with real neighbourhood character
Outstanding live music and boteco scene
Metro station links directly to the centre
cons: Steep hills make daily walking tiring
Take care walking the darker streets late at night

name: Pampulha
tagline: Niemeyer architecture around a lake, well away from the noise
description: Pampulha lies about 8 km north of the centre around an artificial lake ringed by Oscar Niemeyer buildings, a UNESCO listed ensemble. Streets are wide and green, houses have gardens, and the lakeside loop is the city's favourite running and cycling route. The federal university sits on its edge.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads who want space, running routes and a quieter daily rhythm
pros: Lakeside loop for running and cycling every day
Larger homes with gardens for the money
cons: Around 30 to 40 minutes into the centre by car or bus
Public transport links are slow and indirect
Almost no coworking or nomad community out here
